method: Official standards opened with web tool; short paraphrases only. No provider or commercial service contacted.

sources.title: RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security
sources.use: Code flow, exact redirects, confidential-client PKCE recommendation and qualified refresh behavior. Mixer server-session custody and numerical bounds are design choices.

sources.title: RFC 7636: Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients
sources.use: S256, random verifier entropy and published known challenge test vector.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
sources.use: Separate ID-token validation, issuer/subject semantics and pairwise-subject qualification.

sources.title: RFC 9207: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Issuer Identification
sources.use: Compare authorization-response issuer with saved expected issuer before code use.

sources.title: RFC 9068: JSON Web Token Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
sources.use: Resource-token validation remains distinct from OIDC ID-token use; current Mixer compatibility profile is narrower.

sources.title: RFC 6454: The Web Origin Concept
sources.use: Origin comparison includes scheme, host and port; same-origin deployment is a proposed Mixer choice.

sources.title: HTTPWG Cookies: HTTP State Management Mechanism
sources.status: work in progress, October 23 2026 Internet-Draft, not final RFC
sources.use: SameSite and __Host- cookie behavior; browser runtime verification remains pending.

sources.title: RFC 7009: OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation
sources.use: Later provider revocation endpoint, distinct from local session revocation.

sources.title: OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout 1.0
sources.use: Later qualified provider logout endpoint and registered redirect handling.

retrieval_limitations.result: Web tool timed out twice; not relied on or cited. No CORS-standard claim needed for proposed same-origin route policy.
